questions.q: What is the standard dbt fix for a join fanout like this one?
options: Pre-aggregate the many-side of the join down to one row per key before joining
Add a DISTINCT to the final select statement
Switch the left join to an inner join
Delete the duplicate rows manually after each run
questions.explain: Collapsing payments to one row per order_id before the join turns the relationship into the one-to-one one the join was always meant to assume.

questions.q: What does `int_payments__aggregated` do with a split payment's two amounts?
options: Sums them into the order's real total revenue with `sum(amount)`
Keeps only the first payment and discards the second
Averages the two amounts together
Multiplies them together
questions.explain: sum(amount) grouped by order_id correctly combines a split payment into one true total — which is also what Finance actually wanted.

questions.q: Why is `dbt run --full-refresh` required here, not just a plain `dbt run`?
options: fct_orders's existing incremental data already has the duplicated rows baked in; is_incremental()'s filter would leave that old bad data untouched
Full refresh is always required after any model change, as a general dbt rule
Plain dbt run doesn't support changing a ref() inside a CTE
There's no real difference between the two commands
questions.explain: A full refresh re-derives every row under the corrected join; an incremental run would only reprocess new rows, leaving old duplicated rows in place.

questions.q: After the fix, what should happen to Lesson 11's `[Total Revenue]` and Lesson 12's `[Order Count]`?
options: Total Revenue now matches the Snowflake check exactly; Order Count stays unchanged because DISTINCTCOUNT was never actually wrong
Both measures need to be completely rewritten from scratch
Order Count also needs fixing because it was previously wrong
Neither measure is affected by this fix in any way
questions.explain: SUM(amount) was inflated by the fanout and is now corrected; DISTINCTCOUNT(order_id) was already immune to the fanout, as set up back in Lesson 12.

questions.q: Only one part of `fct_orders` changes to apply this fix. What is it?
options: The payments CTE's source — from the raw staging model to the new one-row-per-order aggregate
The unique_key configuration
The is_incremental() block's watermark column
The materialization type, from incremental to table
questions.explain: Everything else about fct_orders — its config, unique_key, and other columns — stays the same; only where the payments CTE reads from changes.
